questions.q: Which body sits at the top of the audit hierarchy in the bank, above the Audit Committee of the Board and the Chairman?
questions.explain: The Hierarchy of Audit in Universe chart places the Board of Directors at the top, above the Audit Committee of the Board and the Chairman.

questions.q: As per the document, what is one stated purpose of inspections and audits conducted in banks?
options: To evaluate the adequacy, completeness, operational effectiveness and efficiency of the control systems in the bank
To fix the annual budget of the branch
questions.explain: The document lists evaluating the adequacy, completeness, operational effectiveness and efficiency of control systems as a key reason inspections and audits are conducted.

questions.q: Under Risk Based Internal Audit (RBIA), major risk areas taken up for risk assessment in branch activities include Credit, Earnings, Operations and which other area?
questions.explain: The document lists the four major risk areas for RBIA risk assessment as Credit, Earnings, Operations and Internal Control.

questions.q: Under RBIA, observations are classified under low, medium and high risk based on which set of loan accounts of the branch?
questions.explain: The RBIA table states observations are classified under low, medium and high risk based on the Top 100 loan accounts of the branch.

questions.q: As per the current year target mentioned in the document, what percentage of branches shall be covered under RBIA, with the rest covered under conventional inspection?
questions.explain: The document states that in the current year 75% of the branches shall be covered under RBIA and the rest as per conventional inspection.

questions.q: Under conventional (regular) inspection, branches are rated using which five-tier scale based on percentage of marks scored?
options: Low, Medium, High, Very High, Extremely High
Poor, Unsatisfactory, Satisfactory, Good, Very Good
questions.explain: The comparison table shows conventional branch inspection rates branches as Poor, Unsatisfactory, Satisfactory, Good and Very Good based on % of marks scored.

questions.q: Under RBIA, a branch with 'High' Business Risk combined with 'Low' Control Risk is graded as which category?
questions.explain: The RBIA grading table shows High Business Risk combined with Low Control Risk results in a 'High Risk Branch' grade.

questions.q: Under RBIA, a branch with 'High' Business Risk combined with 'High' Control Risk is graded as which category?
questions.explain: The RBIA grading table shows High Business Risk combined with High Control Risk results in an 'Extremely High Risk Branch' grade.

questions.q: In the Score/Rating of Control Level table, a score of 80% and above corresponds to which rating?
questions.explain: The RBIA score table shows that a score of 80%+ corresponds to a 'Very Good' rating, indicating a sound and good control environment.

questions.q: Under Regular Inspection grading, a branch scoring 60% and above but below 70% is rated as?
questions.explain: The Regular Inspection range-of-marks table shows 60% and above but below 70% corresponds to a 'Satisfactory' grade/rating.

questions.q: Under RBIA/Regular Inspection periodicity, a Low Risk (Very Good rated) branch must be re-inspected within how many months of the previous inspection?
questions.explain: The Periodicity of Inspection table shows Low Risk/Very Good branches have a previous-inspection period of 18 months.

questions.q: Under the periodicity of inspection table, a branch rated as 'Very High or Extremely High Risk' (or Unsatisfactory/Poor) must be re-inspected within how many months?
questions.explain: The table shows Very High/Extremely High Risk or Unsatisfactory/Poor branches have the shortest inspection period of 9 months.

questions.q: For a newly opened branch, the first inspection findings should be reported to which committee, and within what period?
questions.explain: The document states that for a newly opened branch, first inspection findings (period: 9 months) should be reported to ACE on a quarterly basis.

questions.q: The Offsite Monitoring Cell at Head Office monitors reports that may be reviewed on what frequency basis?
options: Daily, weekly, monthly or quarterly basis
questions.explain: The document states the frequency of these reports may be looked into on a daily, weekly, monthly or quarterly basis.

questions.q: What does the Offsite Monitoring Cell (OMU Cell) at Head Office primarily do?
options: Conduct statutory audit of the bank
Monitor and guide the functioning of the Offsite Monitoring Unit (OMU) at Regional Offices
questions.explain: The document states the Offsite Monitoring Cell at Head Office shall monitor and guide the functioning of OMU at Regional Offices.

questions.q: In addition to key functional areas, what else does the OMU Cell monitor as prescribed by the Chairman/GM from time to time?
questions.explain: The document states the OMU Cell shall monitor key functional areas and the transactions exceeding threshold limit prescribed by the Chairman/GM.

questions.q: A branch is classified as a 'Chronic Defaulter' if it has not submitted periodic audit returns to the Regional Office for how long?
questions.explain: The General Guidelines slide defines a Chronic Defaulter as a branch which has not submitted periodic audit returns to Regional Office for the past three months.

questions.q: A Quick Mortality Account (QMA) is defined as an account that becomes NPA within what time period from the date of first disbursement, for limits sanctioned for the first time?
questions.explain: The document defines a QMA as any account becoming NPA within a period of one year from the date of first disbursement for first-time limits.

questions.q: If a branch reports two or more instances of QMAs with individual book balance of Rs.5.00 lakhs or more during a quarter, who takes this up with RACE to decide on verification of all loans sanctioned by that official?
questions.explain: The document states the Regional Manager shall take up with RACE to decide whether to verify all loans sanctioned by the official in such cases.

questions.q: For a branch categorized as Scale I or II in a rural/semi-urban centre, the follow-up of the Relieving Manager's Certificate for timely submission should occur within how many days from completion of taking charge?
questions.explain: The document specifies that for Scale I & II branches in rural/semi-urban centres, the follow-up period is 4 days from date of completion of taking charge.

questions.q: The Audit Committee of Board (ACB) guides in developing effective policies for which functions?
options: Only Concurrent Audit and IS Audit
Internal Audit, Concurrent Audit, IS Audit and all other inspection and audit functions
questions.explain: The document states the ACB will guide in developing effective Internal Audit (Chairman), Concurrent Audit, IS Audit and all other inspection & audit functions.

questions.q: Which of the following is an item reviewed ANNUALLY by the Audit Committee of the Board (ACB), rather than quarterly?
options: Annual review of Whistle Blower Policy
Quarterly review of Concurrent Audit Reports
questions.explain: The ACB table lists Annual review of Whistle Blower Policy under the 'Annual' column, while the other options are listed under 'Quarterly'.

questions.q: The ACB reviews the status of legal audits conducted for accounts with what minimum exposure, on a quarterly basis?
questions.explain: The document states ACB quarterly reviews the status of Legal Audits conducted for accounts with exposure of Rs.1.00 Crore and above.

questions.q: How frequently must the Audit Committee of Executives (ACE) meet, as a minimum requirement?
options: At least once in a quarter and minimum 6 times a year
questions.explain: The document states ACE should meet minimum at least once in a quarter and minimum of 6 times in a year.

questions.q: Who serves as the Convenor of the Audit Committee of Executives (ACE)?
questions.explain: The document explicitly states that HOD (Inspection & Audit) will be the Convenor of ACE.

questions.q: What is ACE authorized and empowered to approve or ratify, besides other functions?
options: Changes/amendment in the scoring pattern, rating parameters and reporting formats
questions.explain: The document states ACE is authorized and empowered to approve/ratify changes/amendment in the scoring pattern, rating parameters and reporting formats.

questions.q: In the ACE half-yearly review items, which department (HO) is responsible for 'Review on the recovery of amount involved in fraud'?
questions.explain: The half-yearly review table lists 'Review on recovery of amount involved in fraud' under HO: Inspection & Audit.

questions.q: At Regional Audit Committee of Executives (RACE) meetings, whose presence (without delegation) is compulsory?
questions.explain: The document explicitly states Regional Manager (without delegation) is compulsory in RACE meetings.

questions.q: Who chairs the RACE meetings held at Regional Offices?
questions.explain: The document states RACE meetings held at Regional Offices shall be chaired by the IC Head.

questions.q: As per RACE guidelines, what is the maximum number of RACE meetings held in a month, and which branch category is closed at HO instead of RACE?
options: Maximum three meetings a month; Category 'B' branches closed at HO
Maximum two meetings a month; Category 'E' branches closed at HO
Maximum one meeting a month; Category 'A' branches closed at HO
Maximum four meetings a month; Category 'C' branches closed at HO
questions.explain: The document states monthly maximum is two RACE meetings, and branches Category 'E' shall be closed at HO.

quizzes.topic: Inspection Centres, HO Department Roles & Zero Tolerance Areas

questions.q: Which officer grade is designated as In-Charge (MAP) for Inspection Centres?
options: Senior Manager / Manager in Regional Office
questions.explain: The document states one officer in the grade of Senior Manager / Manager in Regional Office will be designated as In-Charge (MAP).

questions.q: Inspection of Training Centres by Inspection Centres is conducted on what basis?
questions.explain: The document states Inspection Centres conduct inspection of Training Centres on a bi-annual basis.

questions.q: The Regional Manager must visit a branch within how many months from the date it is declared High/Very High/Extremely High risk (or Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory/Poorly rated)?
questions.explain: The document states the Regional Manager is to visit the branch within 3 months from the date of declaring the branch under the above risk/rating categories.

questions.q: A 'spurt in advances' flagged for scrutiny is defined as an increase of more than what percentage by number/amount over the previous quarter?
questions.explain: The document defines Spurt in Advances as advances of more than 10% by number/amount over the previous quarter.

questions.q: Which HO department is responsible for co-ordinating the concurrent audit of branches and organizing the empanelment of external auditors?
questions.explain: The document lists co-ordinating concurrent audit and empanelment of external auditors as functions of the HO: Inspection & Audit Department.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a 'Zero Tolerance Area' that must be compulsorily complied with before closure of an inspection report or accepting FRC?
options: Non creation/non registration of mortgage deed (lien on deposits, assignments) or MOD for securities in favour of the bank
Minor discrepancy in stationery stock register
questions.explain: The document lists non-creation/non-registration of mortgage deed or MOD as a Zero Tolerance Area requiring compulsory compliance.

questions.q: According to the Zero Tolerance Areas section, a branch with any zero tolerance deficiency must be rated as high risk and rectified within how many days?
questions.explain: The document states that irrespective of marks obtained, branches with zero tolerance area issues should be rated as high risk, with rectification within 15 days.

questions.q: A fresh slippage of time-barred DPNs is treated as a Zero Tolerance Area issue if the number exceeds 10 or the amount involved exceeds what value?
questions.explain: The document specifies fresh slippage of time-barred DPNs is a zero tolerance issue if more than 10 in number or amount involved is more than Rs.5.00 lakhs.

questions.q: As per the Selection of Staff for Audit System guidelines, for how long should an officer preferably have served as Branch Manager before being considered as an inspector?
questions.explain: The document states the officer should preferably be Scale II and above and have served as Branch Manager for a minimum period of 2 years.

questions.q: Under the SOP for inspectors, within how many working days must inspectors submit their reports?
questions.explain: The document states inspectors submit the reports within 3 working days as part of the SOP.

quizzes.topic: Revenue Audit, Snap Audit & Special Reports

questions.q: Branches with total advances of Rs.1.00 Crore and above (excluding jewel loans and loan on deposits) are subjected to Revenue Audit on what basis?
questions.explain: The document states all branches with total advances of Rs.1.00 Crore and above are subjected to revenue audit on a half yearly basis.

questions.q: Revenue Audit must be completed within what timeframe of the closure of the half year?
questions.explain: The document states Revenue Audit shall be completed within a month of the closure of the half year.

questions.q: Cent percent transaction audit is required where an expenditure head shows an increase of more than what percentage over the previous year?
questions.explain: The document states cent percent transaction audit is to be done where the expenditure head shows an increase of more than 20% over the previous year.

questions.q: Top how many branches (business-wise) as on previous March/September will be subjected to Revenue Audit by Inspection Centres?
questions.explain: The document states the top 100 branches business-wise as on previous March/September will be subjected to Revenue Audit by Inspection Centres.

questions.q: What is the maximum permissible duration for a Snap Audit of a branch?
questions.explain: The document explicitly states Snap Audit may not exceed 2 days.

questions.q: Special Reports submitted by inspectors are addressed to whom, under copy to the IC Head?
options: General Manager (in-charge of Inspection & Audit Department)
questions.explain: The document states inspectors are required to submit Special Reports to the General Manager (in-charge of Inspection & Audit Department) under copy to the IC Head.

questions.q: Special Reports have to be closed within what timeframe from the date of the report?
questions.explain: The document states special reports have to be closed within 2 months from the date of the report.

questions.q: For excess cash found in the Sundry Deposit A/c, amounts less than Rs.100 should be handled how?
options: Credited to customer account after investigation
questions.explain: The document states amounts less than Rs.100 are credited to customer's account after investigation, whereas amounts more than Rs.100 go through RO and are unclaimed for up to 1 year before transfer to income account with permission.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a 'Special Report' trigger under the document?
options: Advances granted by the Branch Manager to close relatives or self without prior HO approval
Branch running out of currency notes
Delayed submission of monthly stationery report
questions.explain: The document lists advances granted by the Branch Manager to close relatives or self without prior approval of Head Office as a Special Report trigger.

questions.q: A branch is treated as 'Very High Risk' or 'Unsatisfactory' due to fraud occurrence if more than how many instances of fraud are reported during a financial year, or if the aggregate fraud amount exceeds a certain value?
options: More than five instances, or aggregate amount more than Rs.5.00 lakhs
More than three instances, or aggregate amount more than Rs.10.00 lakhs
More than one instance, or aggregate amount more than Rs.1.00 lakh
More than two instances, or aggregate amount more than Rs.20.00 lakhs
questions.explain: The document states more than three instances of frauds in a financial year, or aggregate fraud amount more than Rs.10.00 lakhs, results in Very High Risk or Unsatisfactory rating.

quizzes.topic: Closure of Audit Cycle, Management Audit & Credit/Stock Audit

questions.q: The first compliance/rectification reply to an audit report must be submitted within what timeframe from receipt of the audit report?
questions.explain: The document states the first compliance/rectification reply is within one month from the receipt of the audit report, under 'Closure of Audit Cycle'.

questions.q: The Final Rectification Certificate (FRC) must be submitted within what timeframe?
questions.explain: The document states the Final Rectification Certificate (FRC) shall be submitted within two months, under 'Closure of Audit Cycle'.

questions.q: Closure of Credit Audit reports at RO (RACE) level must be completed within how many days?
questions.explain: The document states closure of Credit Audit reports at RO: RACE is within 60 days, and Credit and Inspection are also noted as closed within 60 days.

questions.q: For Management Audit of a Regional Office, what is the man-days requirement and who conducts it?
options: 3 days, by an external CA firm
2 days, by a Senior Manager from other RO/HO along with IC Head
1 day, by the Regional Manager alone
questions.explain: The Management Audit table specifies a Senior Manager from other RO/HO along with IC Head conducts it annually, requiring 2 days.

questions.q: Who closes the Management Audit report of Regional Offices, after which HO: Inspection & Audit places a consolidated review note to ACE and ACB?
questions.explain: The document states Management Audit report of Regional Offices will be closed by the Chairman, with a consolidated review note placed before ACE and ACB.

questions.q: External frauds such as pledge of stolen jewels up to what amount need not result in downgrading of the RBIA rating?
questions.explain: The document states external frauds like pledge of stolen jewels up to Rs.10.00 lakhs need not result in downgrading of the RBIA rating.

questions.q: For Credit Audit, closure of reports is placed to the Chairman by which HO department, in coordination with the IA department?
questions.explain: The document states closure of Credit Audit reports: HO: Credit HOD, IA Department, placed to Chairman, and RO: RACE within 60 days.

questions.q: Besides Statutory Audit by external auditors, the bank is subject to inspection by NABARD on what frequency, and Management Audit by the Sponsor Bank on what frequency?
options: NABARD annually; Sponsor Bank once in two years
NABARD once in two years; Sponsor Bank annually
questions.explain: The document states the bank is subject to Inspection by NABARD annually and Management Audit by the Sponsor Bank once in two years.

questions.q: Which types of audit are named directly under 'Types of Audits' in the document, alongside Revenue Audit and Credit Audit?
options: Staff Accountability Study, IS Audit, Compliance Audit, Jewel Verification, Snap/Special Audit, Pre-Release Audit, Stock Audit
Marketing Audit, HR Audit, Legal Audit
questions.explain: The 'Types of Audits' slide lists Revenue Audit, Staff Accountability Study, IS Audit, Compliance Audit, Jewel Verification, Snap/Special Audit, Pre Release Audit, Credit Audit and Stock Audit.

questions.q: Compliance Audit is conducted at what point in the audit cycle?
options: After receipt of FRC, before acceptance for closure of report
questions.explain: The document states Compliance Audit occurs after receipt of FRC (before acceptance for closure of report).

questions.q: Software Audit is generally carried out utilising the services of officers holding which qualification?
questions.explain: The document states Software Audit shall be carried out generally utilising the services of CISA qualified officers of the bank.

questions.q: Application software audit under IS Audit is carried out by which type of empaneled auditors?
questions.explain: The document states application software audit is carried out by CERT-In empaneled auditors (Computer Emergency Response Team).

questions.q: Network Audit under IS Audit is conducted on what frequency, using CISA/CISSP qualified officers?
questions.explain: The document states Network Audit is conducted on an annual basis using CISA/CISSP qualified officers attached to the core team of IS Audit.

questions.q: Under the IS Audit rating and reporting scale, a score below 50% is rated as which risk category?
questions.explain: The document states for IS Audit rating, a score below 50% is rated High Risk, 50-70% Medium Risk, and above 70% Low Risk.

questions.q: Other IS Audit coverage such as aggregation points (routers & switches), AEPS/POS, ATM, third-party IT environments and Data Centre is conducted on what frequency?
questions.explain: The document states IS Audit of aggregation points, ATM, third-party IT environments, Data Centre, CBS Project Office, DR site, CTS Centre, Regional Offices is annual, while Administrative Departments are bi-annual.

questions.q: VAPT (audit) of critical applications like Internet Banking and Mobile Banking should be conducted at what minimum frequency?
questions.explain: The document states VAPT of critical applications - Internet Banking, Mobile Banking - is to be audited at least half yearly.

questions.q: Which of these is listed as a Special Report item under IS Audit?
options: Lack of awareness in maintaining password secrecy
questions.explain: The document lists lack of awareness in maintaining password secrecy as one of the IS Audit Special Reports items.

questions.q: Maintenance of which type of account in a branch, other than those permitted by the system, is flagged as an IS Audit special report item?
questions.explain: The document lists maintenance of parking account in branch, other than those permitted by the system, as an IS Audit special report concern.

questions.q: Branch Audit under IS Audit types corresponds to what activity?
questions.explain: The document states under 'Various Types of Information Systems Audit', Branch Audit corresponds to Regular Inspection.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as an IS Audit special report concern regarding daily checks?
options: Non-checking of VVR, SWO & other critical reports on a daily basis
questions.explain: The document lists non-checking of VVR, SWO and other critical reports on a daily basis as an IS Audit special report item.

questions.q: Staff accountability for lapses in an advance account must be examined within how many years of the relief of the officer concerned?
questions.explain: The document states staff accountability for lapses in advance account is to be examined within 4 years of the relief of the officer.

questions.q: Staff accountability examination should be completed at least how long before the retirement of the staff member?
questions.explain: The document states staff accountability at least 3 months before the retirement of the staff should be examined.

questions.q: For which category of large value NPA accounts must a copy of the staff accountability study report be forwarded to the CVO and the Sponsor Bank?
options: Accounts with book balance of Rs.1 Crore and above
Accounts with book balance of Rs.50 lakhs and above
All NPA accounts regardless of value
Accounts with book balance of Rs.5 Crore and above
questions.explain: The document states all large value NPA accounts with book balance of Rs.1 Crore and above where staff accountability study is conducted require a copy sent to CVO and the Sponsor Bank.

questions.q: Which committee is convened by HOD Vigilance Department and consists of heads of Recovery, Accounts, Credit and Planning departments, for staff accountability?
questions.explain: The document states the Internal Advisory Committee (IAC) consists of heads of Recovery, Accounts, Credit and Planning departments, with HOD Vigilance as convenor.

questions.q: For non-credit related staff accountability issues involving exposure up to Rs.1.00 lakh, which authority handles the report?
options: Chairman level HO Staff Accountability Committee
GM level HO Staff Accountability Committee
Regional Staff Accountability Committee (RSAC) headed by RM
questions.explain: The competent authority table shows exposure up to Rs.1 lakh is handled by the Regional Staff Accountability Committee (RSAC) headed by RM.

questions.q: For non-credit related issues with amount involved above Rs.15.00 lakhs, which authority is the competent authority for staff accountability reports?
options: Chairman level HO Staff Accountability Committee
GM level HO Staff Accountability Committee
questions.explain: The competent authority table shows amounts above Rs.15.00 lakhs are handled by the Chairman level HO Staff Accountability Committee.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as one of the triggering credit-area events for staff accountability study?
questions.explain: The document lists account slipping to NPA category as one of the trigger events (along with filing of suit, OTS, adverse audit findings) for staff accountability study.

questions.q: Which of these is listed among the 'Non-Credit Areas' warranting staff accountability study?
questions.explain: The document lists non-compliance to KYC/AML/CFT guidelines as a non-credit area item warranting staff accountability study.

questions.q: The staff accountability study for advance accounts is based on outstanding balance excluding which component?
questions.explain: The document states the staff accountability study is based on the outstanding balance excluding MOI.

questions.q: If a staff accountability lapse is identified in a study report but not reported in the inspection reports, who is held responsible?
questions.explain: The document states that if the staff accountability study report was not reported in inspection reports, the respective inspecting official/s would be held responsible.

questions.q: Concurrent Audit coverage must ensure at least what percentage of deposits and advances of the bank on an ongoing basis?
questions.explain: The document states coverage of at least 50% of deposits and 50% of advances and other risk exposure of the bank under concurrent audit is to be ensured on an ongoing basis.

questions.q: Branches with average advance figure of less than what amount may be exempted from concurrent audit coverage?
questions.explain: The document states branches with average advance figure of less than Rs.10.00 Crore may be exempted from concurrent audit coverage.

questions.q: Concurrent Audits are conducted by which external parties?
questions.explain: The document states concurrent audits are conducted by external Chartered Accountants / retired bank officials.

questions.q: Under concurrent audit, the report of the month is due by when, and closure of reports is expected within what period?
options: End of succeeding month; closure within 1 month
15th of succeeding month; closure within 3 months
5th of succeeding month; closure within 2 months
10th of succeeding month; closure within 1 month
questions.explain: The document states the report of the month is due before the 5th of the succeeding month, with closure of reports within 2 months.

questions.q: The tenure of a Concurrent Auditor is initially for how long, extendable for a further period, subject to satisfactory performance?
options: One year, extendable for a further two years (overall three years)
Six months, extendable for six months
Two years, extendable for a further one year
questions.explain: The document states the tenure of concurrent audit would be initially for one year and would be extended for a further period of two years (overall three years), based on performance.

questions.q: Retired officers considered for initial engagement as concurrent auditors must have retired on superannuation within the last how many years, in Scale II and above?
questions.explain: The document states officers who retired on superannuation in Scale II & above within the last three years may be considered for initial engagement as concurrent auditor.

questions.q: What is the maximum permissible age for a retired officer to continue as concurrent auditor, including being assigned another branch from the 4th year onwards?
questions.explain: The document states the retired officer can be assigned another branch in the 4th year onwards within the maximum permissible age of 65 years.

questions.q: As part of Concurrent Auditor's role, how many jewel packets should be randomly verified every month?
questions.explain: The document states random verification of 20 number of jewel packets every month is part of the Concurrent Auditor's role.

questions.q: As per fees structure, what is the concurrent audit fee for a branch with total business between Rs.50 crore and up to Rs.100 crore?
questions.explain: The Concurrent Audit fee table shows Rs.9000 for total business above Rs.50 crore and up to Rs.100 crore.

questions.q: Stock Audit / Credit Audit of a branch shall NOT be allotted to which auditor for that same branch?
options: The Concurrent Auditor of the same branch
The IS Auditor of the branch
questions.explain: The document states Stock Audit/Credit Audit shall not be allotted to the Concurrent Auditor of the same branch, to maintain independence.
